engagement to bring Hensoldt’s agentic AI under enforced authority on the

objectives: Bring the existing RFI/RFQ agent under explicit authority bands with signed, replayable evidence — defensible at customer and regulator review.
Provide a faster, regulator-defensible candidate-screening shortlist (conditional on works-council approval) to support the ~9,000-hire growth direction.
Automate routine SAP procurement or engineering-change decisions inside policy, freeing senior time for the decisions that matter.
Stand up one reusable enforcement layer — Decision Contracts, Crypto Passport signing, Flight Recorder telemetry — that subsequent agents inherit.
Produce EU AI Act Article 43/47 documentation as a by-product of running on the platform.

identity.subtitle: HENSOLDT — agentic AI under enforced authority
identity.tagline: Three MVPs to build now · one held in reserve · two procurement routes

runs.t: Hensoldt is scaling hard — a direction of roughly
9,000 hires over three years
(about 3,000 a year) — on a heavy SAP estate, and your team has already built an RFI/RFQ agent on
Microsoft Copilot Studio and LangGraph
. The appetite to move is real: the sponsor would, in his words, rather start yesterday than today.
Two things sit between intent and production. First, the existing build runs
without enforced authority bounds or signed evidence
— it commits without explicit limits, and its audit trail can't be reconstructed on demand. Second, a
Betriebsrat (works council) approval — expected 27 July 2026
— is required before anything moves beyond demo and proof-of-concept into production.
This pre-read frames
three use cases worth building now
, a fourth held in reserve,
two procurement routes
, and a path to begin ingestion on contract signature so work is underway before the works council decides on production.

sections.t: MVP 1 — RFI/RFQ governance (#39 + #94) · live in one week

runs.t: Reverse-engineer your existing Copilot Studio + LangGraph build straight into the platform — no rebuild. Map every decision point, surface where the agent commits without authority bounds and where evidence isn't signed, then encode
authority bands (€100k, one geography, one line) as a Decision Contract
. Every decision is Crypto Passport–signed and audit-ready within the week. EU AI Act: limited risk.
The work is yours; the enforcement is ours.

sections.t: MVP 2 — Candidate screening (#58) · conditional · Annex III high-risk

runs.t: Rank and recommend,
never reject

— a human signs every decision. Article 14 oversight enforced at the gateway; disparate-impact telemetry on every cohort; drift triggers re-certification; per-candidate reasoning artefact, replayable and discloseable. Benchmark impact: time-to-shortlist
30+ days → 5–7 days
, recruiter throughput
— material against the 9,000-hire target. Held
conditional
on Betriebsrat approval (27 July) and the sponsor's appetite for leading with a high-risk case; Alex has flagged this as politically sensitive.

sections.t: MVP 3 — SAP wedge, one of two · scoped with the SAP transformation lead

runs.t: A · Source-to-PO.
Indirect-material sourcing to a signed PO, inside policy, on SAP MM. Routine in-policy POs 3–5 days → under 1 hour; 40–60% straight-through; maverick spend enforced at the gate.
B · ECR/ECO engineering change.
Triage to ECCB-approved on SAP PLM, with ITAR/AWG export-control screening at the gate. Triage cycle 2–4 weeks → 24–48 hours; defence-grade audit at the source.

Both reuse the same authority pattern as MVP 1, proven on SAP elsewhere (a German industrial supplier, indirect-material procurement). The A-or-B choice is confirmed with your SAP transformation lead.

sections.t: Backup — IT-security cloud-evaluation auto-check · held in reserve

runs.t: Raised on the 2 June call as a “phenomenal, quick-win” agentic case: the IT-security
cloud evaluation sheet
is a binary, repetitive control check with a clear decision contract — approve when criteria are met, hard-reject and escalate to IT Security otherwise. Low blast radius,
no works-council exposure
— the natural fallback if the sponsor declines to lead with candidate screening.

sections.t: 3.  Why this is safe to do
NO PASSPORT = NO EXECUTION. Agents execute, but every high-stakes action is gated by a signed Crypto Passport bound to a current Decision Contract. No valid passport, no commit.

runs.t: Runtime-neutral.
We govern your Copilot Studio and LangGraph builds in place — no rip-and-replace. Define the agent once, run it on either, even side by side.
EU AI Act by-product.
Articles 43 and 47 documentation falls out of running on the platform — not a separate compliance project.
Evidence by default.
Every action carries a replayable, signed audit trail — defensible at customer and regulator review, in minutes rather than hours.
Delivery model: Novagentica-built.
We design, certify, and deploy; Hensoldt owns the outcomes.
No pilots
— MVP 1 is production from day one, then MVP 2 and MVP 3 follow as incremental releases on the same enforcement layer.
Each MVP runs across the three planes:
Architect (design).
Domain → outcomes → functions → teams → agents; charters and playbooks.
Authority (govern).
The Decision Contract, signing keys, and EU AI Act risk class.
Control (operate).
Deployment to the runtime, the fail-closed execution gateway, Flight Recorder telemetry, drift detection and re-certification.
No agent reaches production until it passes the
three-tier AQVP certification
— a technical quality gate, not a commercial sign-off. Credentials live in the vault; Architect is never in the execution path.
Put both routes to the sponsor and let priority and the enlisted-provider position decide. They are
not mutually exclusive
— Route 2 can fast-track the start while Route 1 settles the production contract.
